text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Latency SLO breach detected for customer 'Driftwood Financial' (VPC: eu-west-2). p99=3.8s (SLO 2.5s). Affected: dedicated-pool-3, tenant driftwood-prod. PagerDuty triggered to oncall.

mike-oncall: acked PD, jumping in. what's customer impact? @lina-support can you confirm if they're seeing errors or just slowness?

lina-support: CS: slow checkout flow for EU users reported, clients timing out around ~4s. No 500s reported yet. Customer on call but asked for status updates.

jessica-sre: quick metric snapshot — dedicated-pool-3 token p99 spike starts ~10:07 UTC. GPU queue depth rose from 12 -> 60, GPU util steady ~78%, kernel-run latencies increased. Looks like queuing on runtime.

julian-eng: note: there was a model swap to 'llama-ensemble-v2' on that pool at 09:55 UTC as part of today's rollout. rolling back?

mike-oncall: runbook step: attempt tenant isolation first (route Driftwood to warm spare). I will perform traffic move to avoid noisy-tenant impact.

mike-oncall: running command: 
```
redwoodctl route update --tenant driftwood-prod --from pool:dedicated-pool-3 --to pool:dedicated-warm-7 --weight 100 --dry-run=false
```

incident-bot: action queued: route update submitted by mike-oncall (run_id=run-8791). Audit link: https://console.redwood/run/run-8791

cloudops: warm pool dedicated-warm-7 capacity OK: 1200 concurrent tokens, current load 150. Autoscaler will add one extra node in ~90s if needed.

tom-cse: starting canary at 10:20 UTC — shifting 10% traffic first, watching p95/p99 per-tenant.

lina-support: CS notified customer: "We're routing your traffic to a warm instance to restore latency. We'll update every 10 minutes." They acknowledged.

jessica-sre: after routing, overall p99 for Driftwood dropped to 2.1s within ~3m (observed 10:23). Tenant-specific p99 ~1.9s. Queuing metrics dropped, request concurrency normalized.

julian-eng: seeing some sessions fall back to llama-ensemble-v1 during routing — investigate model v2 kernel path. Might be regressed kernel selection on certain sequence-lengths.

mike-oncall: keep mitigation in place. Collect artifacts for postmortem: logs, perf profiles, kernel timings. Who can grab flamegraphs and model op traces?

julian-eng: collecting flamegraphs now:
```
scp ops@perfbox:/var/logs/driftwood/2026-03-15-10* ./
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf-driftwood-10-23.svg
```

jessica-sre: I pulled runtime traces and KV-cache hit patterns. v2 shows heavy attention kernel stalls around 512-768 token windows. Suspect a codepath that disables an optimized kernel.

lina-support: customer confirms perceived latency returned to normal, no further user complaints since 10:25.

mike-oncall: preparing oncall handoff at 11:00 UTC to jessica-sre. Severity reduced from S1->S2. Opening follow-up ticket RW-4598 for rollback/analysis.

jessica-sre: ack handoff. Action items: 1) validate kernel selection heuristics for v2; 2) add perf smoke to deployment CI; 3) add explicit canary perf thresholds to rollout pipeline; 4) update runbook with warm-pool switch checklist.

lina-support: scheduling customer readout for tomorrow 13:00 UTC, adding notes and timeline.

incident-bot: RESOLUTION NOTE: Mitigation successful — traffic routed to dedicated-warm-7, p99 within SLO for Driftwood Financial. War room closed at 11:05 UTC. Follow-ups tracked in RW-4598.

mike-oncall: closing notes: probable immediate cause = model-variant regression under specific sequence-length distribution causing kernel fallback/queuing. Long-term: perf gates in deploy, better canary telemetry, and a safer warm-pool eviction policy. :memo:
